metadata.disclaimer: VALIDATION SCOPE NOTICE: HeatWave Guardian's validation evaluates biometeorological accuracy (Liljegren WBGT), IMD heatwave criteria adherence, and operational decision-support recommendations. It does NOT validate individual clinical heat illness or predict mortality.
limitations: Reanalysis spatial resolution (~25km) leads to smoothing of extreme localized point temperatures.
ERA5 exhibits documented pre-monsoon cold bias (~ -1.55°C) across continental Indian heatwave epicenters.
Validation applies to biometeorological parameters and ISO 7243 work-rest guidance; does not predict individual clinical heat illness.
Urban heat island (UHI) microclimate amplifications are not captured without localized on-site sensors.

environmental_metrics.population_evaluated: Station observatories and 0.1°-0.25° atmospheric cells across 6 Indian states
environmental_metrics.note: Negative bias reflects documented ERA5 reanalysis cold bias in peak pre-monsoon maximums over the Indian subcontinent.

classification_metrics.unit_of_analysis: Daily maximum synoptic declaration vs IMD criteria

insights: Temperature-Only fails to capture compound humidity risks (e.g. Coastal Mumbai 35°C with 80% RH produces severe WBGT 31.8°C).
IMD regional criteria adjusts for climatological norms across Plains (40°C), Coastal (37°C), and Hills (30°C).
Liljegren WBGT accounts for wind convective dissipation and direct solar radiation flux.
Integrated HeatWave Guardian adjusts recommendations for metabolic workload, PPE restriction, and acclimatization.

forecast_backtest.limitation: Historical forecast backtesting is strictly performed where genuine archived NWP model runs exist. Current forecast API outputs are never substituted for past archives.

peak_window_backtest.summary: Evaluated 4 hourly cases: 100.0% elevated period detection rate with average peak hour difference of 0.0 hours and 0 false alarms on control baseline.

humidity.finding: Removing dynamic humidity altered WBGT by >=1.0°C in 60 of 80 (75.0%) scenarios, critically misclassifying coastal and humid-plains heat.

wind.finding: Removing wind modulation altered thermal stress in 19 of 80 (23.8%) scenarios by eliminating convective sweat evaporation.

solar_radiation.component: Solar Radiative Heat Flux (Outdoor Direct Sun)
solar_radiation.finding: Removing direct solar radiation underestimated outdoor heat burden by 1.5–3.5°C WBGT across all daytime outdoor scenarios (50.0% impact).

workload.finding: Differentiating Light vs Heavy metabolic intensity altered work-rest schedules or risk tiers in 64 of 80 (80.0%) scenarios.

acclimatization.finding: Accounting for unacclimatized status escalated caution in 64 of 80 (80.0%) borderline and elevated heat conditions.

ppe.finding: Vapor-barrier impermeable PPE triggered severe escalation across 64 of 80 (80.0%) scenarios due to total sweat entrapment.

recovery_environment.finding: Providing air-conditioned cooling vs compromised recovery altered action levels or work-rest guidance in 43 of 80 (53.8%) scenarios.

cases.name: Khammam Severe Pre-Monsoon Heatwave (May 2015)
limitations: ERA5 25km grid averages localized station extreme (43.9°C reanalysis vs 48.0°C station peak).
Relative humidity derived via Magnus-Tetens formula from dewpoint temperature.

cases.name: Hyderabad Urban Heatwave & Spatial Smoothing Boundary Case (May 2015)
limitations: Coarse spatial resolution (~25km) blunts intense urban microclimate station spikes by 2.5–4.4°C.

cases.name: Delhi NCR Northern Plains Extreme Heatwave (May 2024)
limitations: Extreme hot-dry inland conditions with very low afternoon RH (15–25%).

cases.name: Mumbai Coastal Hot-Humid Thermal Stress Event (May 2023)
limitations: High marine boundary layer moisture impairs evaporative sweat dissipation.

cases.name: Ahmedabad Landmark Arid Heatwave (May 2016)
limitations: Arid western climate with dry desert wind (Loo).

cases.name: Bengaluru Southern Plateau Non-Heat Control (Jan 2023)
limitations: Mild plateau climate; temperatures 24–28°C; zero heatwave expectation.
